title: Davis Library and the campus core, UNC Chapel Hill
_comment_bbox: Davis Library plus the campus core that gives it context: Polk Place and the quad to the west, Wilson Library, the Student Union and the Pit to the south, Lenoir. About 720 x 810 m. A library alone would read as a building floating in space, which is the failure the Union Square brief warns about.
_comment_frame: Origin is the Walter Royal Davis Library footprint centroid, OSM way 44343213 — a physically identifiable object, per the new-world skill. originElevationM 144.35 from USGS EPQS on 2026-09-03 (value 144.349411011, NAVD88). gridBearingDeg 97.405 is the length-weighted axial (doubled-angle) mean over 3.47 km of South Road, East Cameron Avenue, Raleigh Street, Country Club Road and Stadium Drive — the same method used for the Union Square grid fit. The campus core sits about 7.4 degrees off a true E-W grid.

sources._comment: The point of the A/B. OSM way 44343213 carries neither a height nor a building:levels tag, so a baseline build has nothing to extrude Davis Library from.
Chapel Hill's campus core drops toward the Pit and Lenoir; a flat plate would misread the site badly.

Measured building heights from the 3DEP point cloud. Declared AFTER osm-overpass because it needs the footprints. This is what settles Davis Library: OSM is silent, Overture says 11.73 m for an 8-floor building, the lidar measures the roof.
